D.E. Shaw Interview Experience
Ravi Maurya  |  T.Y. B.Tech IT 2019-23
For 2022 Summer Internship (On-campus)
04th September 2021
DE Shaw India (DESIS) visited our campus for Internships for 3rd Year students. A total of
201 students had applied for this.
Online Coding Round (1st Sept, 2021)
An online test was conducted on HackerRank. Total time was around 95 minutes and
consisted of 3 Coding Questions:
Q.1) You have been given an N-sized array of product numbers and another N-sized
array of the product cost for those N elements respectively. There can be multiple
products of the same product number with different costs. You need to find the maximum
cost we can get by selecting one product of each product number. So you cannot select
multiple products of the same product number.
Eg.
product_num = [1,2,3,2,4,4,6,1,1,1]
cost = [3,6,1,2,8,9,10,4,5,2]
Output: 31
Explanation: We have 4 units of product 1 with the highest cost of 5
2 units of product 2 with the highest cost of 6
1 unit of product 3 with the highest cost of 1
2 units of product 4 with the highest cost of 9
and 1 unit of product 6 with the highest cost of 10

5 + 6 + 1 + 9 + 10 = 31
I made an array of pairs {product number, cost} and sorted this. And for each product
number selected the highest cost and added all.
(Passed all test cases)
Q.2) You are given an NxM matrix. The cells contain *(asterisk) or .(dot)
Here, * means land and . means water.
You need to find the maximum one of all the minimum area rectangles that can
completely enclose an island. Neighboring * forms an island (Top, Left, Right, Bottom).
The minimum area rectangle can have water in it but should contain an island completely
within itself.
Eg.
* * * . . .
* * . * . .
. . * * . .
. * * . * *
. . . . . *
Output: 9
Here, there are 3 islands.
Topmost island is
* * *
* *

The minimum area required to cover it will be 3*2 = 6
The middle island is
*
* *
* *
The minimum area required to cover it will be 3*3 = 9
The bottom island is
* *
*
The minimum area required to cover it will be 2*2 = 4
The maximum out of these will be 9.
This was similar to the Number of Islands problem, I used DFS on the matrix. For each
island, I maintained Top, Left, Right, Bottom boundaries and updated them for each DFS.
Area will be (Right- Left+1) * (Bottom - Top + 1).
(Passed all test cases)
Q.3) You have been given N strings, you need to create a minimum length string such
that those N strings are substrings of that output string.
Extra condition: Let’s consider 2 strings A and B from the given list, if A is before B in the
list then in the output string, B should start after the start of A.
Eg.
[abc, bcfgh, ghtyok, cfghght]
Output: abcfghtyokcfghght

Explanation:
S = abc
S = abcfgh
S = abcfghtyok
For the final string cfghght , even though some part of it occurs in S we cannot consider
that as it is starting before the start of the previous string in the array (ghtyok)
S = abcfghtyokcfghght
Solved this greedily, took one string at a time, and tried to fit it within the main string
following that extra condition.
(Passed all test cases)
I was able to solve all 3 questions with all test cases passed.
From 201 students who applied for the online test from our college, 10 students were
shortlisted for the next round.
Technical Round 1 (4th Sept 2021, 9 AM)
This round was conducted on Hackerrank CodePair. There were two interviewers. The
best thing was they don’t want you to code. They just want to know your approach to the
questions.
What was asked?
Introduce Yourself.
Then he immediately jumped to coding questions.
Q.1) Merge N sorted arrays into one sorted array. (Available on GeeksforGeeks)

I gave them a bruteforce solution (Append all elements to the new array and then sort
the new array) and explained the Time complexity for that. Then I gave another approach
that was a little more efficient.
Then I thought of improving it further and came up with an approach of merging arrays in
groups of 2. (Check GeeksForGeeks for this) But then I took some time to figure out the
Time complexity for that and also got confused in some parts. But finally gave the correct
Time Complexity.
Q.2) Given a list P of probabilities of size N which adds to 1. Create a function that can
randomly return a value i in the range 0 to N-1 with the probability of P[i].
Eg. [0.3, 0.5, 0.2]
The random function returns 0 with a probability of 0.3, 1 with a probability of 0.5, and 2
with a probability of 0.2. So this is like a biased function.
I started by asking a lot of questions to clarify it as the question was very weirdly framed.
After getting all the info I started coming up with approaches.
The first few approaches I thought were completely wrong in the sense of probability, the
interviewer directly didn’t point that out but gave hints. Slowly I came to the correct
approach taking some help from them. Typically this question was super easy, but I took
a lot of time to think about it.
The final approach was:
Generate random numbers between 0 and 1 using a built-in random function.
If it falls between 0 and 0.3 then return 0.
If it falls between 0.3 and 0.8 then return 1.   (Why 0.8?   0.3 + 0.5 = 0.8)
If it falls between 0.8 and 1.0 then return 2.
Q.3) Create your own data structure which supports Insertion, Deletion, Search and
GetRandom each with O(1) time complexity.   (GeeksForGeeks)

Actually, this is a very famous question, but I had somehow never seen this before.
I started thinking about LinkedList as Insertion, Deletion is O(1).
To also support Search, I thought of using Linked List along with Hashmaps. Still, this
doesn’t satisfy GetRandom in O(1).
Thought of Queue, Deque, Stack. But none of them fit.
Also thought of Array along with HashMaps, but Deletion won’t be O(1). Spent a lot of
time thinking about this. The interviewer gave hints that: try to think about Deletion once
again.
After spending more time, I came up with the final approach using Arrays + Hashmap.
(Refer GeeksForGeeks)
It was a very easy question if you knew what and how to do it, but I took a lot of time as I
saw it for the first time.
After this the other interviewer asked me some OOPs related basic questions:
-
Difference between classes and objects
-
Static variables in C++ and real-life use
-
Inheritance concept
Then he asked me If I had any questions. I asked when this pandemic occurred then how
a massive company like DE Shaw moved online. He said that DE Shaw had systems and
infrastructure already developed for such situations. So they were already prepared for it
and didn’t face too many problems.
That’s it. This interview ran for about 1 hour. Overall my performance was not good
according to me as I took a lot of time for those coding questions even though we didn’t
need to write the code, only an explanation. I was sure that I won’t be shortlisted for the
next round.
But luckily I got shortlisted for the next round. Out of 10 students, 5 were shortlisted for
the next round. The next round was on the same date after a few hours.

What saved me? I think even though I was slow, I was speaking and explaining to him all
the time. I think this factor mattered more than whether I can solve questions fast or slow.
Technical Round 2 (4th Sept, 1:30 PM)
We thought that this might be an HR Round, but this one was also a Technical Round.
What was asked?
Introduce yourself.  Basic info about my project.
Then he asked me what subjects have been taught in our college and which languages I
like.
I told him that DSA, OOPs, OS, DBMS were taught and I prefer C++ for CP and Javascript
for Web Dev. He looked at my Resume that I had mentioned Java also. So he asked me
whether I knew Java. I honestly told him that I have worked with Java in the past, but I’m
not very proficient with the syntax and only understand the concepts and I normally
Google the syntax whenever I am making something with Java. (Never tell lies in an
interview, always be honest)
Then he started with DBMS first.
DBMS
He told me Let’s suppose you are running a business and there are a lot of Employees
working there. You need to maintain their info in a database. He asked me what
attributes I will be storing. (Gave him like 10-12 attributes). Then we started discussing
each attribute. All along with this conversation, I ended up making a lot of changes to the
DB. Added many tables, foreign keys, Normalization, etc.
Then he asked me some common queries I would like to have on my DB as an HR
Manager. And told me to write SQL queries for them (again they didn’t care about syntax,
I was writing Pseudo SQL queries xD)
There were lots of concepts like Joins, GroupBy, Order, etc used here. Then he asked me
common questions on Indexing, Normalization, Joins, Transactions, Keys, etc. (Study all
these concepts well and try to explain them with examples)
He was pretty satisfied with all my answers.

OS
Now we started with Operating Systems. He asked common questions like Process vs
Threads, Multicore and Multiprocessor systems, Scheduling, What is the advantage of
Threads ( we had a long discussion on this ), Virtual memory concept, Deadlocks and
what we generally do for deadlocks, Fragmentation( Internal, External, Solutions), Paging
( Use, Replacement Algos ), Thrashing, Segmentations, etc.
He was pretty much satisfied with everything.
OOPs
He asked some basic OOPs concepts like Inheritance, Compositions, Abstraction,
Encapsulation, Virtual Methods, etc.
He wrote some pseudo-code (which looked like Javascript xD) and asked me some C++
concepts like Runtime Polymorphism, etc.
This section also went well.
Coding Question:
There were 3 questions:
Q.1 ) Minimum value within each window of size k in an array.  (GeeksForGeeks)
I knew this question already,
Started with bruteforce and gave its time complexity. Then explained the optimal
approach.
Q.2) Can’t remember this one. But it was also a medium-level question. But the follow-up
to that was about HashMaps. And how Maps and Hashmaps are different. How they are
implemented.
I was able to answer this but was not able to correctly answer “Why maps are preferred
over Hashmaps” as I think Hashmaps are better.
Q.3) There is a graph of N nodes, we have no info about that. No info about which nodes
are connecting whom. You have been given a function canReach(a,b) which returns true

if we can reach from a to b else returns false. You need to think of a way to minimize the
use of canReach and know which node is the source. A source node can reach all other
nodes, but no other node can reach the source node.
Told them the brute force way to check each node with every other node.
If canReach(a, b) returns true then we can reach from a to b. This means b can never be
the source node.
Then check for canReach(a, c). If this returns false then a can never be the source node.
Now directly jump to c as we have already eliminated the possibility of a and b being
source nodes.
This will be an O(n) solution.
At last, he asked me if I had any questions for them, I asked about how DE Shaw
operates and how they conduct the Internship Process. He explained to me the entire
process in detail. (Always ask a question at the end, gives the impression that you are
interested in this company)
Overall this round was good. The interviewers were amazing, very calm, and helpful. It
felt more like a discussion with a friend than an Interview.
We thought there would be another round (HR Round), so I started studying for that. But
luckily there were no further rounds.
At about 9 PM we got the results. Out of 5 students in the Last Round, 3 were selected
for the Internship and I was fortunate to be one of them.

Tips:
For Coding Test:
1)
Practice famous problems from 450dsa.com, GeeksForGeeks, and Leetcode.
2)
If the test consists of CS Fundamentals, then study for them thoroughly. Few questions
are generally a bit easy.
3)
If the test contains Aptitude questions, they generally include Probability, PnC,
Logic-based, Statistics, Math based puzzles, etc. Practice some questions from IndiaBix
website.
(For DE Shaw, only Coding Questions are there)
For Interviews:
1)
The most important thing is to stay calm and be confident. A lot of weightage is on your
confidence.
2)
While explaining something, use your hands, freely move them around. This helps a lot to
gain confidence as well as adds a positive impression on the Interviewers.
3)
Don’t stop talking. Yes! Explain everything continuously. Even if you are not sure of your
solution, tell them. Even if you are thinking, think aloud. Going silent gives a bad
impression.
4)
Join the interview link at least 2-3 minutes before the given time. Gives an impression that
you are punctual.
5) Put the phone to silence. Make sure you give your interviews in a silent environment.
Background noises can distract you as well as the interviewer.
6) Memorize the “Introduce yourself” answer by heart. Even though it seems very obvious,
sometimes due to pressure we may forget it.
7)
After giving the approach for a problem, mention its time and space complexity by
yourself. Don’t wait for the interviewer to ask about it.
8)
While explaining CS Fundamentals, always try to give a real-world example if possible for
that concept. Gives a positive impression.
9) Always ask a question to your interviewer at the end. This makes them feel that you are
interested in this company.
10) Do not cheat in Interviews by any means or tell any lies, the interviewers are very clever
enough to detect that. Be confident, honest, and have trust in yourself.

Resources I followed:
1)
450dsa.com   :   Solve all questions if possible or atleast the main ones from each section.
2)
OOPs   :
Object Oriented Programming CheatSheet - by Love Babbar (whimsical.com)
3)
DBMS    :
DBMS RoadMap - by Love Babbar (whimsical.com)
4)
SQL    :     Refer W3Schools
5) OS    :
Operating System CheatSheet [by Love Babbar] (whimsical.com)
6) CN     :
Networking Cheatsheet [By Love Babbar] (whimsical.com)
ALL THE BEST!!! (Keep faith in yourself and your preparation)
